katas.title: Agent PR: let the CSV import send ARR as text

seededDefectKey.scenario: POST /api/deals with projectedArr -500, 0, or an empty CSV cell (which z.coerce.number() turns into 0).
seededDefectKey.consequence: The type change also dropped .positive(), so negative and zero ARR pass validation and reach approvals and the leaderboard totals: the "negative pipeline" bug the old test was written for. The change the brief needs is z.coerce.number().positive().

seededDefectKey.scenario: The only test on this boundary failed against the new code, and the PR changed the test instead of the code: its input went from -500 to "not-a-number" and its name changed to match.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The suite is green only because nothing asserts the negative case any more. A test edited in the same PR as the code it guards has to keep its old assertion; the string input deserves a new case next to it.

katas.title: Agent PR: make deal transitions conflict-safe with a compare-and-set status update (review finding 1)

seededDefectKey.scenario: Any transition: a partner submits, a sales rep approves, a manager rejects or closes a deal.
seededDefectKey.consequence: dealRepository has no compareAndSetStatus: the call throws a TypeError inside the transaction, every transition rolls back and the route answers a generic 500. TypeScript would refuse the call; npm test is vitest run, which strips types without checking them, so a green run proves nothing about it.

seededDefectKey.scenario: What the repository really offers: listDeals, findVisibleById, createDeal, updateStatus and createApproval, and updateStatus writes where { id } only.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The status-guarded write the PR relies on does not exist and is not added by it. The fix needs it in this PR: an update filtered on id and the expected status, with a 409 when it matches no row.

katas.title: Agent PR: stop the 500s for DEAL_DESK users (their role has no row in the permission matrix yet)

seededDefectKey.scenario: A session whose role has no row in the matrix (DEAL_DESK, or any role value the code does not know) moves a deal from SALES_APPROVED to APPROVED.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The lookup throws, the catch logs a warning and answers true, so that role passes every permission check: it can submit, give both approvals and close deals. The error the PR silences was the only thing refusing it.

seededDefectKey.scenario: Where the 500 really came from: the matrix is the one list of who may do what.
seededDefectKey.consequence: A new role needs its own row here (or a deliberate 403), and a failed permission lookup must fail closed. A catch that logs and carries on turns a crash into an authorization bypass.

katas.title: Agent PR: add a test that a partner seller cannot give the sales approval (plus a small cleanup)

seededDefectKey.scenario: A partner admin sends a deal that sales rejected back into review (REJECTED -> SUBMITTED).
seededDefectKey.consequence: The transition table now lets a rejected deal back into the approval flow, and submitting needs only deal:submit, which every partner role holds: rejection is no longer final. Nobody asked for that, and it rides in a PR described as a test and a cleanup.

seededDefectKey.scenario: What resubmitting does to the stored deal.
seededDefectKey.consequence: updateStatus clears rejectionReason on every transition that is not a rejection, so the resubmitted deal loses the reason it was rejected for; only the DealApproval history row keeps it.

katas.title: Agent PR: only the assigned sales rep or channel manager may move an assigned deal (review finding 3)

seededDefectKey.scenario: Before this PR (the shipped code, review finding 3): a deal is assigned to sales rep A, and sales rep B approves it, because the domain checks the role only.
seededDefectKey.consequence: This is the defect the PR closes, not one it adds. The check runs before the transaction, leaves platform admins and unassigned deals as they were, and is the review's own fix (solution F) applied to both stages; findVisibleById already returns both assignee fields. Approve it.

katas.title: Agent PR: test that a sales rep cannot give the channel approval

seededDefectKey.scenario: Before this PR: the domain suite has one case, the DRAFT -> APPROVED jump; no test asserts that a role is refused a stage it does not hold.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The PR fills that gap correctly: SALES_REP lacks deal:approve_channel in the matrix, and the expected message is exactly what assertPermission throws. A test-only PR with a true assertion deserves an approval, not invented comments.

katas.title: Agent PR: tidy the transition rules into one permission table (no behaviour change)

seededDefectKey.scenario: A channel manager rejects a SALES_APPROVED deal; a sales rep rejects a deal that is waiting for the channel approval.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The table keys the permission on the target status only, but who may reject depended on the current one. Rejecting now always needs deal:approve_sales: the channel manager gets a 403 at the stage they own, and a sales rep can reject at the channel stage, overruling the channel manager.

katas.title: Agent PR: the leaderboard job uses the deal's close-date quarter (review finding 6), plus a naming tidy-up

seededDefectKey.scenario: A deal is approved on 2026-09-30 (2026-Q3) with a close date of 2026-11-15 (2026-Q4).
seededDefectKey.consequence: The job now rebuilds the 2026-Q4 snapshot, but the leaderboard counts an approved deal in the quarter of its approvedAt, so the deal belongs to 2026-Q3, whose snapshot this approval no longer refreshes: Q3 stays stale and Q4 is rebuilt for nothing.

seededDefectKey.scenario: Why finding 6 cannot be fixed in the job alone: the counting query filters on approvedAt.
seededDefectKey.consequence: The review asks for the close-date quarter, but moving only the job splits the refresh from the count. Both move together (job and query) or neither does, and which date a leaderboard should use is a product question to raise, not a one-line change.
